title: Render an image and save it
summary: Look through the camera, render a still image with F12 and save it as a picture file.

steps.say: Make sure the top left of the 3D viewport says Object Mode. Press Tab if it says Edit Mode.

checks.prompt: Does the mode selector at the top left of the 3D viewport read Object Mode?

hints: The mode selector is the first drop-down in the strip above the 3D view.
Click the selector and choose Object Mode.
steps.why: Renders show the scene as it looks in Object Mode.

steps.say: With your mouse over the 3D viewport, press Numpad 0 to look through the camera.

checks.prompt: Does the 3D viewport now show a darkened border around a lighter frame, with Camera Perspective written at the top left?

hints: Use the 0 on the numeric keypad.
Or click the camera icon below the axis ball at the top right of the viewport.
steps.why: The camera view shows exactly what will appear in the render.

steps.say: Press F12 to render. A Blender Render window opens and the picture builds up.

checks.prompt: Is a separate Blender Render window open showing a rendered image of the scene?

hints: On some laptops F12 needs the Fn key held down.
Or open the Render menu at the top left and choose Render Image.
steps.why: Rendering turns the scene into a finished image from the camera's point of view.

steps.say: Wait until the render finishes. The progress text at the top of the render window stops changing.

check.prompt: Does the Blender Render window show a complete image with no progress bar still running?

hints: A simple scene takes a few seconds. Say done when the image looks finished.
Press Escape to stop a render that takes too long.
steps.why: Saving before the render ends would save an unfinished picture.

steps.say: With your mouse over the render window, press Shift Alt S to open Save As.

checks.prompt: Is a Blender file browser open, with a file name field and a save button at the bottom?

hints: Still renders are not saved on their own. This step writes the file.
Or open the Image menu at the top left of the render window and choose Save As.
steps.why: The render only lives in memory until you save it.

steps.say: Pick a folder, type a file name in the field at the bottom, then click the save button at the bottom right.

checks.prompt: Has the file browser closed, leaving the render window showing the image again?

hints: Pressing Enter in the file name field also saves.
The file format, PNG by default, is set in the panel on the right side of the file browser.
steps.why: Choosing the place and name yourself means you know where the picture is later.

steps.say: Close the render window with the X at its top right corner.

check.prompt: Is the Blender Render window gone, leaving the main Blender window in front?

hints: Your saved image stays on disk after the window closes.
Press F11 later to bring the last render back.
steps.why: The render window can always be reopened, so closing it loses nothing.
